name: AccuRanker
subcategory: keyword research, backlinks and rank tracking
tagline: Run a small compliant rank tracker with transparent snapshots and alerts

pricing.notes: Typical 1,000-keyword monthly package; exact tiers can change.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 2,000 keywords on the current default selector; daily updates.
tiers.notes: Annual price is calculated exactly from the official 10% annual discount.

tiers.name: Expert
tiers.limits: Keyword quantity is selectable; the accessible page did not expose the default count; includes unlimited read API.
tiers.notes: Annual price is calculated exactly from the official 10% annual discount.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: More than 25,000 keywords; unlimited users and domains.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual is 10% lower; plan can be changed or cancelled at no cost
pricing.hiddenCosts: price scales with the selected keyword quantity, so the $224 and $764 cards are not universal fixed costs across every volume

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For AccuRanker, run a small compliant rank tracker with transparent snapshots and alerts. The hard boundary is high-frequency global rank data, scale, integrations, and reporting reliability, plus proprietary web index and data acquisition.
coreLoopDIY: Track a user-supplied keyword set, collect permitted search-result snapshots at low volume, alert on changes, and show rank trends without pretending to recreate a commercial web index.
requirements: approved search-data API or manual imports
whatYouLose: high-frequency global rank data, scale, integrations, and reporting reliability
moatNotes: proprietary web index and data acquisition
ongoingBurden: proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for AccuRanker because customers pay for a continuously refreshed web-scale dataset whose collection cost dwarfs the dashboard around it. The recurring cost buys proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: SerpBear
priorArt.desc: Open-source search ranking tracker for owned keyword sets.

alternatives.name: OpenSEO
alternatives.desc: Tracks desktop and mobile positions by location with history; free software, compulsory DataForSEO credits.

alternatives.name: SerpBear
alternatives.desc: A real tracker with history and alerts; the software is free, the Google results usually are not.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SEO PowerSuite Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Free forever, provided you never save a project; that is a demo with better stamina, not rank tracking.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Serposcope
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Once the obvious free answer; archived in 2024, last commit January 2022, and the maintainer says bugs will not be fixed.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SerpTrail
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A neat new tracker from SerpApi; 42 stars and a July launch make it evidence, not yet a recommendation.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the 1,000 keywords plan and a small owned-keyword tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for AccuRanker in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Playwright, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track a user-supplied keyword set, collect permitted search-result snapshots at low volume, alert on changes, and show rank trends without pretending to recreate a commercial web index.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create projects with domains, keywords, target country, language, device, and tags.
Fetch rankings only through the configured compliant API and enforce a daily budget.
Store raw result snapshots and normalized positions so every chart is auditable.
Display current rank, movement, best rank, URL changes, and a compact SERP history.
Import backlink and keyword files from third-party tools without claiming independent coverage.
Add scheduled runs, failure alerts, CSV export, retention settings, and database backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out building a general web crawler or backlink index.
Deliberately leave out circumventing search-engine access controls.
Deliberately leave out traffic estimates presented as observed first-party data.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
